source: Vinokurova N. Lexical Categories and Argument Structure: A Study with Reference to Sakha. Utrecht, 2005. (LOT Dissertation Series, no. 103)
topic: Extending H&K's proposal to denominal verb formation in Sakha
notes: What is ungrammatical is the LAA-counterpart of (12) in which –LAA has attached to the upper, locative noun ‘shelf’. The LAA-counterpart of (11) is o.k. with –LAA attaching to the lower noun ‘saddle’. –LAA does have the ability to attach at the level of LocP as witnessed by (10): in (10a) –LAA is suffixed to the noun ‘town’ which is merged in the specifier of LocP in (10b), the lexical verb paraphrase of (10a). Therefore the reason behind ungrammaticality of (6b) lies not in the attachment possibilities of –LAA but rather in the fact that if –LAA attached at the level of LocP in (12), the lower noun would remain unlicensed. This suggests that if –LAA attached to ‘book’ in (12) (abstracting away from the presence of the lexical verb), the result would be grammatical as confirmed by (13).
en: Ergis put a book/books on the shelf.
